subtitle: Networks of Stone and Ink: How the Satavahanas Held the Deccan Together

panels.shot: sweeping bird's-eye view over Pratishthana on the Godavari, fading into routes stretching across the Deccan
panels.action: Śivakhaṇḍila stands on a terrace in Pratishthana, scroll in hand, as dusty roads radiate from the city toward distant aharas under a vast Deccan sky.

dialogue.text: From Pratishthana’s river markets to far aharas like Govardhana, the Satavahanas ruled not by a single iron chain, but by many braided roads of officers, allies and written promises.

i18n.hi: प्रतिष्ठान के नदी-बाज़ारों से गोवर्धन जैसे दूर आहरों तक, सातवाहन लोहे की एक ज़ंजीर से नहीं, अफ़सरों, साथियों और लिखी शर्तों की कई गुंथी राहों से राज करते थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in over the Godavari at dawn, boats clustered near a bustling riverfront town
panels.action: Mist hangs over the Godavari as boats crowd a lively quay, warehouses and tiled roofs of Pratishthana rising behind the riverbank.

dialogue.text: A Greek sailor wrote of Paethana, an inland mart where carts brought gems and cotton. The same place, in Prakrit, was Pratishthana, heart of a Deccan realm that the West barely understood.

i18n.hi: एक यूनानी नाविक ने पैथाना का ज़िक्र किया, भीतर का बाज़ार जहाँ गाड़ियाँ रत्न और कपास लाती थीं। वही जगह प्राकृत में प्रतिष्ठान थी, उस दक्कनी राज्य का दिल जिसे पश्चिम मुश्किल से समझता था।

panels.shot: medium interior shot inside a royal hall, slightly low angle to show authority
panels.action: Śivakhaṇḍila stands in a pillared hall of Pratishthana, before a low dais where unseen royals sit, as a scribe kneels nearby with palm-leaf and stylus.

dialogue.text: Here, in Pratishthana’s halls, orders were not simply barked and obeyed. They were weighed, negotiated, copied onto leaf and stone, and carried outward by men like Śivakhaṇḍila.

i18n.hi: यहीं, प्रतिष्ठान के महलों में, हुक्म बस झट से नहीं चलते थे। तौले जाते, सौदे होते, पत्तों और पत्थर पर लिखे जाते, और शिवखण्डिल जैसे लोग उन्हें बाहर तक ले जाते।

panels.shot: close-up on Śivakhaṇḍila’s hands holding a rolled grant, background blurred
panels.action: Śivakhaṇḍila’s steady hands cradle a sealed palm-leaf charter, the faint impression of a royal emblem visible on its binding thong.

dialogue.speaker: satavahana_administrators
dialogue.text: A grant once given is a promise carried by many eyes, not just mine.

i18n.hi: एक बार दिया हुआ दान, सिर्फ़ मेरी नहीं, कई आँखों से निभाया गया वादा है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Deccan road, caravan moving, administrator riding alongside
panels.action: Śivakhaṇḍila rides beside a small escort along a dusty track, a bullock cart with chests and scroll-bundles trundling behind across the scrubland.

dialogue.text: From Pratishthana he rode westward, toward the Govardhana ahara near Nashik, carrying royal words that would remake villages without a single soldier’s sword being drawn.

i18n.hi: प्रतिष्ठान से वो पश्चिम की ओर निकला, नाशिक के पास गोवर्धन आहर की तरफ़, ऐसे शाही हुक्म लिए जो बिना तलवार निकले गाँवों की सूरत बदल देते।

panels.shot: wide shot of Nashik hill with caves, slightly high angle to show terrain and monastery
panels.action: The rocky hill of Nashik rises, its façade pierced by orderly rock-cut caves, as Śivakhaṇḍila and attendants approach along a winding path below.

dialogue.text: Near Govardhana, monks carved quiet worlds into stone. Cave by cave, donors left records on the walls: merchants, queens, and officers like Śivakhaṇḍila, binding monastery and state.

i18n.hi: गोवर्धन के पास, भिक्षु पत्थर में शांत दुनिया काट रहे थे। गुफ़ा-दर-गुफ़ा दानदाताओं के नाम दीवारों पर उकेरे गए: व्यापारी, रानियाँ, और शिवखण्डिल जैसे अफ़सर, जो मठ और राज्य को बाँध रहे थे।

panels.shot: intimate interior wide shot inside Nashik Cave 3, walls visible, light slanting in
panels.action: Inside a rock-cut hall, Śivakhaṇḍila stands with folded hands before seated monks, while a mason traces lettering lines on a smoothed stone panel.

dialogue.text: There, in Cave 3, his name was cut into living rock. The inscription spoke of villages assigned, of revenues diverted, of powers withheld from officials yet unborn.

i18n.hi: वहाँ, गुफ़ा ३ में, उसका नाम ज़िंदा पत्थर पर काटा गया। लेख में बाँटे गए गाँवों की बात थी, मोड़े गए लगान की, और उन अधिकारों की, जो अभी पैदा भी न हुए अफ़सरों से भी छीन लिए गए थे।

panels.shot: close-up on stone surface with incised Brahmi letters, Śivakhaṇḍila’s shadow falling across
panels.action: Brahmi letters appear in neat lines on the stone wall, Śivakhaṇḍila’s faint profile and the mason’s hand hovering beside the unfinished text.

dialogue.text: The grant declared: certain villages, their fields and taxes, set apart. Royal officers, constables, even future police were forbidden to enter, to fine, to interfere.

i18n.hi: दान में लिखा था: कुछ गाँव, उनकी ज़मीनें और कर, अलग किए गए। शाही अफ़सर, दरोगा, यहाँ तक कि आने वाला पुलिस भी, घुसने, जुर्माना लेने, दख़ल देने से रोके गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Śivakhaṇḍila speaking quietly with local headmen outside the cave, temple trees behind
panels.action: Under a spreading tree, Śivakhaṇḍila gestures calmly as village headmen in simple cloth listen, some anxious, some thoughtful, with the cave mouth behind them.

dialogue.speaker: satavahana_administrators
dialogue.text: Your grain goes now to the monastery as the king commands. But your quarrels you must settle yourselves.

i18n.hi: तुम्हारा अनाज अब राजा के हुक्म से मठ को जाएगा। मगर झगड़े अपने तुम्हें ही सुलझाने हैं।

panels.shot: split-depth shot: foreground village fields, background a distant fortified hill with local chief’s banners
panels.action: Śivakhaṇḍila stands at the edge of green fields, while far off a hill-fort flies the banners of a local maharathi, hinting at another power behind the land.

dialogue.text: Yet these villages did not float alone. Behind them stood maharathis and mahabhojas, old Deccan lords with forts, horses, and their own coins flashing royal names beside theirs.

i18n.hi: फिर भी ये गाँव अकेले नहीं तैरते थे। उनके पीछे महारथि और महाभोज खड़े थे, पुराने दक्कनी सरदार, जिनके क़िले, घोड़े और अपने सिक्के थे, जिन पर राजा का नाम उनके साथ चमकता था।

panels.shot: medium shot in a courtyard, Śivakhaṇḍila meeting a richly dressed local chief, both flanked by retainers
panels.action: In a sunlit courtyard, Śivakhaṇḍila bows slightly to a jeweled local lord seated on a low platform, while spear-bearing retainers and scribes stand behind each side.

dialogue.text: The Satavahana king needed such men. They were not humble clerks but partners, sometimes in-laws, sometimes rivals. Administration in the Deccan was a negotiation, not a flat chain of command.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन राजा को ऐसे ही लोगों की ज़रूरत थी। ये मामूली मुंशी नहीं, हिस्सेदार थे—कभी ससुराल, कभी दुश्मन। दक्कन की हकूमत सीधी ज़ंजीर नहीं, खींचतान वाली सौदेबाज़ी थी।

panels.shot: close-up on a Satavahana coin and a local chief’s coin side by side on a low table
panels.action: Two silver coins rest on a wooden surface: one bearing a Satavahana royal name, the other showing a local title alongside a royal symbol, as Śivakhaṇḍila’s hand points between them.

dialogue.speaker: satavahana_administrators
dialogue.text: Your face may shine on the coin, lord. But the lion on it still belongs to Pratishthana.

i18n.hi: मुद्रा पर चेहरा तुम्हारा हो सकता है, स्वामी। पर उस पर का सिंह अभी भी प्रतिष्ठान का है।

panels.shot: dynamic montage-like wide shot of different figures across the Deccan, linked by implied roads
panels.action: A wide scene shows a general drilling troops, a kumara in a roadside town, a monk in a cave, and Śivakhaṇḍila reading a scroll, all connected by winding roads across a map-like landscape.

dialogue.text: Mahasenapatis guarded frontiers, kumaras governed districts, merchants funded monasteries, and village elders kept order. The ahara was their shared stage, not a mere field for royal orders.

i18n.hi: महासेनापति सीमा पर तैनात, कुमार ज़िले संभालते, व्यापारी मठों को धन देते, और गाँव के बुज़ुर्ग क़ायदा रखते। आहर सबका साझा रंगमंच था, सिर्फ़ राजहुक्म का मैदान नहीं।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of Pratishthana hall again, Śivakhaṇḍila reporting to a royal figure in silhouette
panels.action: Back in the Pratishthana hall, Śivakhaṇḍila kneels with a scroll unrolled, speaking to a seated royal silhouette, while another scribe tallies notes on a palm-leaf bundle.

dialogue.text: Śivakhaṇḍila returned with news: revenues re-routed, a cave endowed, a local lord appeased. The king heard of harmony as much as of obedience, for both kept the Deccan calm.

i18n.hi: शिवखण्डिल लौट आया खबरों के साथ: लगान की राहें बदलीं, एक गुफ़ा को दान मिला, एक स्थानीय सरदार मान गया। राजा ने सिर्फ़ फ़रमाबرداری नहीं, मेल-मिलाप की भी कहानी सुनी, क्योंकि दोनों से ही दक्कन शांत रहता था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Pratishthana market street, merchants, weavers, foreign traders visible, Śivakhaṇḍila walking through
panels.action: Śivakhaṇḍila walks through a crowded market street of Pratishthana, past bales of cotton, bead-sellers, and a few foreign traders with different dress near packed carts.

dialogue.text: Inland from sea-ports, Pratishthana’s streets thrummed with cloth, beads and wine. Foreign traders saw only a bustling mart; administrators saw the fragile web of agreements that made it possible.

i18n.hi: समुद्री बंदरगाहों से भीतर, प्रतिष्ठान की गलियाँ कपड़े, मनके और मदिरा से गूँजती थीं। विदेशी को बस भागता बाज़ार दिखता; अफ़सरों को वो नाज़ुक जाल दिखता जो समझौतों से टिका था।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Śivakhaṇḍila gazing at the Godavari at dusk, thoughtful profile
panels.action: At dusk, Śivakhaṇḍila stands on the riverbank, watching the Godavari’s dark waters flow, his face quiet, scroll-tube hanging at his side.

dialogue.speaker: satavahana_administrators
dialogue.text: Roads and rivers remember us longer than any shout in a court.

i18n.hi: रास्ते और नदियाँ हमें अदालत की किसी भी चीख से ज़्यादा देर तक याद रखती हैं।

panels.shot: epic high wide shot panning from Pratishthana out over the Deccan, ghosted inscriptions and routes overlaying the land
panels.action: The view rises above Pratishthana, revealing the broad Deccan plateau dotted with forts, caves, villages and faint lines of roads, as translucent scripts in Brahmi seem to float over the landscape.

dialogue.text: Long after the Satavahana court fell silent, Cave 3 still speaks of aharas, officers and immunities. It reminds us that empires endure not by commands alone, but by networks of trust, bargain and stone.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन दरबार की आवाज़ थम जाने के बहुत बाद भी, गुफ़ा ३ अब भी आहरों, अफ़सरों और छूटों की कहानी कहती है। वो याद दिलाती है कि साम्राज्य सिर्फ़ हुक्म से नहीं, भरोसे, सौदे और पत्थर के जाल से टिकते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: Networks of Stone and Ink: How the Satavahanas Held the Deccan Together
subtitle_i18n.hi: पत्थर और स्याही के जाल: सातवाहनों ने दक्कन को कैसे बाँधे रखा
